title: Selected ancient Roman, Roman-Frankish, Gallican and insular manuscript book states

traditions.label: Veronese collection of Roman sacramentary libelli
traditions.scope: The surviving Verona codex as a collection, rather than a complete or universally imposed early Roman missal.
traditions.coverage_note: Its manuscript copying and seventh-century continuation are separate from the composition dates of the collected prayers.

traditions.label: Old Gelasian sacramentary witness
traditions.scope: The one manuscript now divided between Vatican Reg. lat. 316 and Paris lat. 7193 ff. 41–56.
traditions.coverage_note: The catalogue date is for the surviving copy, not the origin of every stratum or papal authorship.

traditions.label: Frankish Gelasian sacramentary witnesses
traditions.scope: The identified Gellone manuscript state; other Frankish Gelasian books remain separate candidates.
traditions.coverage_note: Mixed Roman, Frankish and Gregorian material is attested in the witness; this dossier does not supply an archetype or a descent edge.

traditions.label: Gregorian sacramentary manuscript witnesses
traditions.scope: Identified Cambrai, Trento and Padua codices, each represented by its own manuscript state.
traditions.coverage_note: The named books are distinct witnesses; the Roman exemplar, their copying dates, corrections and supplements must not be collapsed into one institutional event.

traditions.label: Gallicanum Vetus sacramentary parts
traditions.scope: The two separately dated sacramentaries bound in Vatican Pal. lat. 493.
traditions.coverage_note: Two copy dates are shown; the binding date and historical relationship between the parts are unresolved.

traditions.label: Bobbio manuscript sacramentary
traditions.scope: The main BnF lat. 13246 sacramentary, with its separately described inserted Mass and additions.
traditions.coverage_note: Bobbio is a find place, not an established place of composition or a recension label.

traditions.label: Stowe manuscript Mass book
traditions.scope: The Mass and pastoral-rite codex within RIA D.ii.3, distinct from its bound Gospel extracts.
traditions.coverage_note: The later corrections and inserted leaves are known but not dated or collated here as a separate revision state.

sources.title: Earlier Latin Manuscripts, CLA 4.514, Verona LXXXV (80)
sources.inspection: Read shelfmark, palaeographic date, contents, script commentary and separate seventh-century continuation at fol. 139.
sources.limitations: Catalogue description, not manuscript-image collation; it does not date the underlying libelli or establish public liturgical use of the codex.

sources.title: Earlier Latin Manuscripts, CLA 1.105, Vatican Reg. lat. 316 and Paris lat. 7193
sources.inspection: Read both shelfmarks, VIII med dating, contents and account of the Paris leaves separated from the Vatican codex.
sources.limitations: The catalogue's 726–775 interval dates manuscript copying; competing narrower scholarly datings and text strata remain unresolved.

sources.title: Earlier Latin Manuscripts, CLA 5.**105, detached Gelasian appendix
sources.inspection: Read the Paris ff. 41–56 identification and explicit statement that they are the appendix of Reg. lat. 316.
sources.limitations: Confirms one manuscript in two holdings, not two independent book states; images were not collated.

sources.title: Biblissima/BnF description of Paris Latin 12048, Gellone Sacramentary
sources.inspection: Read the shelfmark, last-quarter-eighth-century dating, codicological contents, mixed liturgical description and ninth-century addition at f. 1.
sources.limitations: Aggregated BnF catalogue description; no direct page-image or formula collation. The catalogue's account of textual mixture does not establish the exact source of each prayer.

sources.title: USUARIUM 2219, Cambrai MS 164 (159), Sacramentarium Hadrianum
sources.inspection: Read identity, shelfmark, distinction between proposed Aachen master copy in 790–800 and actual Cambrai copy in 812–813, and indexed Mass contents.
sources.limitations: The 812–813 copying date competes with other palaeographic datings recorded in the inventory; the catalogue is not direct manuscript collation.

sources.title: USUARIUM 6537, Trento cod. 1590, Gregorian Tridentinum
sources.inspection: Read manuscript shelfmark, 800–850 age, title, indexed Mass Ordinary and Canon, and catalogue's Salzburg-model note.
sources.limitations: Catalogue content headings are not a complete manuscript collation; the reported Salzburg model is not proved as a direct exemplar here. The 1985 edition is a modern scholarly publication.

sources.title: USUARIUM 6612, Padua Cathedral MS D. 47, Gregorian Paduense
sources.inspection: Read shelfmark, 830–870 age, reported 840–855 compilation, contents headings, corrector and later Verona appendix notices.
sources.limitations: Compilation estimate, copying range and undated correction/appendix are different roles. The 1927 and 2005 editions are modern scholarship, not ninth-century stages.

sources.title: Earlier Latin Manuscripts, CLA 1.92, Pal. lat. 493 ff. 1–18
sources.inspection: Read folio extent, sacramentary identity, first-half-eighth-century script dating and statement that another later sacramentary is bound with it.
sources.limitations: Catalogue does not date the binding or establish a shared exemplar with the second part; manuscript images were not collated.

sources.title: Earlier Latin Manuscripts, CLA 1.93, Pal. lat. 493 ff. 19–99
sources.inspection: Read folio extent, sacramentary identity, second-half-eighth-century script dating and separate earlier part.
sources.limitations: Catalogue does not establish when the two parts were joined or how their texts relate; manuscript images were not collated.

sources.title: USUARIUM 957, Pal. lat. 493 liturgical contents index
sources.inspection: Read indexed Mass, initiation and Holy Week headings and the catalogue's 1958 edition notice.
sources.limitations: The aggregate USUARIUM age 675–725 does not represent the separate copy dates of both parts; indexed headings cannot allocate every formula to a part.

sources.title: Earlier Latin Manuscripts, CLA 5.653, Paris lat. 13246, Bobbio Missal
sources.inspection: Read eighth-century date, sacramentary contents, separate inserted Mass ff. 251–253 and added matter ff. 1–8, 253v–254, 291v–295.
sources.limitations: Bobbio is documented find place; southeast French origin is a catalogue probability. Neither that probability nor the title establishes Celtic or Roman ancestry.

sources.title: Earlier Latin Manuscripts, CLA 2.268, Stowe Missal core
sources.inspection: Read RIA shelfmark and ff. 12–67 extent, ca. 792 dating with 780–820 bounds, and notice of later corrections and inserted leaves.
sources.limitations: The approximate core-copy date does not date the later Móel-Cáich revision or the origin of its prayer texts.

sources.title: Irish Script on Screen, RIA MS D ii 3
sources.inspection: Read institutional metadata and description separating eleven Gospel folios from the fifty-six-folio Mass, baptism, sick visitation and communion manuscript.
sources.limitations: Institutional record dates the composite broadly to the eighth–ninth centuries; original images were not used for a textual collation.

sources.title: Biblioteca Apostolica Vaticana, DigiVatLib images and record of Reg. lat. 316, Sacramentarium Gelasianum
sources.inspection: IIIF manifest (522 canvases; holding-library metadata title Sacramentarium Gelasianum, date 'Sec. VIII in.') read; images viewed at 1000 px: ff. 3v–4r (canvases 0018–0019: arcade and cross frontispiece; incipit 'In nomine Domini Iesu Christi Salvatoris incipit liber sacramentorum Romanae aecclesiae ordinis anni circuli' with 'Orationes et preces'), ff. 131v–132r (canvases 0274–0275: second frontispiece; 'Incipit liber secundus orationes et preces de nataliciis sanctorum'), ff. 245r–v (canvases 0507–0508: penitential prayers ending in the explicit 'Explicit liber sacramentorum. Deo gratias' and scribe's verse; 245v blank with show-through and quire signature).
sources.limitations: Six named folio images only; no complete page-by-page review, prayer collation or palaeographic dating by this lane. The detached Paris ff. 41–56 (BnF lat. 7193) were not reached because Gallica returned HTTP 403. The holding library's 'Sec. VIII in.' and ELMSS's VIII med. (726–775) remain competing catalogue datings.

sources.title: Biblioteca Apostolica Vaticana, DigiVatLib images of Pal. lat. 493, Missalia Gallicana vetera; Canones
sources.inspection: IIIF manifest (226 canvases, ff. 1a–4a and 1–106; record title 'Missalia Gallicana Vetera; Canones') read; images viewed at 1000 px: front note (canvas 0001), f. 1r (canvas 0010: acephalous Mass for Germanus 'antestitis et confessoris', later marginal 'Missa Romana'), ff. 18r–19v (canvases 0044–0047). F. 18v ends mid-sentence in a creed exposition in a large uncial-type hand; f. 19r begins mid-prayer ('…da illi misericordiam tuam…per lavacri regenerationem') in a different script and layout and then heads 'Incipit exorcismus'.
sources.limitations: Named images only; the scribal change at ff. 18v/19r and the textual break on both sides are direct observations, not a palaeographic dating, a binding date or a demonstration of how many leaves are lost. The Heidelberg mirror (digi.ub.uni-heidelberg.de) presented an Anubis bot challenge and was not used.

sources.title: e-codices, St. Gallen, Stiftsbibliothek, Cod. Sang. 348 (Gelasian Remedius Sacramentary): images, record and Scherrer 1875 description
sources.inspection: IIIF manifest metadata (Chur, around 800, 376 pages; incomplete; at St Gall by about 850) and TEI of Scherrer 1875 p. 122 read. Images viewed: p. 32 (decorated incipit 'In nomine sanctae Trinitatis incipit liber sacramentorum anni circuli Romanae ecclesiae'), p. 368 (Sanctus, Te igitur with 'una cum famulo tuo papa nostro ill. et antistite nostro ill.' and a reference mark to a red-capital foot entry 'Memento Domine famuli tui Remedii episcopi et…'), p. 10 (Masses for the vigil and feast of St Gall, by another hand within Scherrer's pp. 9–20 group).
sources.limitations: Three page images and the library descriptions; no complete prayer collation. The core copying date comes from catalogues (ELMSS 796–824; e-codices 'around 800'); the front St Gall Masses and later corrections are not separately dated here.

sources.title: Earlier Latin Manuscripts, CLA 7.936, St Gallen Stiftsbibliothek 348
sources.inspection: Read shelfmark, Rhaetian minuscule, VIII ex–IX in (796–824) date, origin probably Chur, contemporary red-uncial Remedius commemoration at the foot of p. 368, presence at St Gall by the second half of the ninth century, and correction throughout by a St Gall scholar in that period.
sources.limitations: Catalogue description; the attribution of corrections to Abbot Hartmut is the catalogue's probability and is not adopted as a dated event.

sources.title: E. A. Lowe (ed.), The Bobbio Missal, vol. I, Facsimile (Henry Bradshaw Society 53, 1917), registered complete scan
sources.inspection: Registered repository artifact ia-facsimile-vol-1-697f4c50 (SHA-256 697f4c50…1023, 616 PDF pages) re-read locally. Plate sequence starts at PDF 13 = f. 1r. PDF 511–512 = f. 250r–v in the main hand; PDF 513–517 = ff. 251r–253r, carrying the photographed folio numbers 251–253 and a different, more regular hand beginning 'Deus regum atque cunctorum regnorum…' with petitions for 'principem nostrum'; PDF 518 = f. 253v, a smaller cursive later hand.
sources.limitations: A 1917 collotype facsimile of BnF lat. 13246, not the original or current Gallica images (Gallica HTTP 403). The plate-to-folio mapping was checked at the photographed folio numbers on PDF 513–517 and assumed only between them. No prayer collation of the core or the added matter was made.

sources.title: Irish Script on Screen, RIA MS D ii 3 (Stowe Missal) page images
sources.inspection: IIIF manifest (149 canvases; scribes recorded as Sonid and Máel Caích; provenance note on Tallaght/Lorrha) read; images viewed at 1000 px: f. 12r (decorated 'Peccavimus Domine' opening of the Missal with a heading added in the upper margin by another hand), f. 37r (communion antiphons with alleluia followed by the signature 'Moel Caich scripsit' in the same pointed hand), f. 37v (postcommunion 'Quos caelesti Domine dono satiasti' and thanksgiving in a larger, rounder hand).
sources.limitations: Three folio images only. The hand change and signature are direct observations; which leaves Máel Caích inserted or rewrote, and when, is not determined from these images.

stages.label: Verona collection of Roman sacramentary prayers
stages.date_label: manuscript copied in the second half of the sixth century (551–600)
stages.scope: Verona Biblioteca Capitolare LXXXV (80), the surviving collection of sacramentary material; seventh-century continuation distinguished from the core.
stages.summary: An identifiable sixth-century codex attests collected liturgical prayers. ELMSS separately identifies a continuation on f. 139 by a seventh-century hand.

evidence.locus: Shelfmarks; Date; Contents; Script Commentary, f. 139
evidence.claim: Identifies the codex, dates its principal script VI², and distinguishes the later continuation.

stages.limitations: The 551–600 coordinate is a palaeographic copying range, not the composition of the libelli or a date of Roman promulgation. The collection is not shown to be a complete missal or a public-service exemplar; no folio-level text checked.
stages.reception: The catalogue reports a later Verona connection, not evidence that this codex or collection was universally received in Rome.

stages.label: Old Gelasian manuscript in two present holdings
stages.date_label: manuscript copied in the early to middle eighth century (BAV record 'Sec. VIII in.'; ELMSS VIII med., 726–775)
stages.scope: The surviving sacramentary Reg. lat. 316 and its detached Paris appendix, not a complete reconstruction of earlier text strata.
stages.witness_label: Vatican Reg. lat. 316 with Paris BnF lat. 7193 ff. 41–56
stages.summary: The catalogue treats the Vatican and Paris portions as one eighth-century codex with sacramentary, exorcism and penitential contents. Original images confirm the incipit naming a liber sacramentorum Romanae aecclesiae ordinis anni circuli (f. 4r), a decorated opening of Book II for the saints (f. 132r) and the explicit of the Vatican volume (f. 245r).

evidence.locus: Shelfmarks; Date; Contents; Origin and Provenance
evidence.claim: Dates and identifies the Vatican codex and its detached Paris portion.
Calls the Paris leaves the appendix of the same Gelasian manuscript.

evidence.locus: ff. 3v–4r (DigiVatLib canvases 0018–0019); ff. 131v–132r (0274–0275); f. 245r–v (0507–0508); record metadata
evidence.claim: Original images show the book's own title for a Roman sacramentary of the year's cycle, the separately decorated opening of its second book of saints' feasts, and the explicit closing the Vatican volume after penitential prayers; the holding library dates the codex 'Sec. VIII in.'.

stages.limitations: The year bounds now span both catalogue datings (BAV 'Sec. VIII in.'; ELMSS VIII med., 726–775); neither is adopted over the other. The Paris appendix leaves were not image-checked (Gallica HTTP 403). Neither Pope Gelasius's authorship, the date of individual prayers, nor direct descent into later Gelasian books follows from this witness. Wilson's 1894 critical edition is not an ancient stage.
stages.reception: Surviving Frankish manuscript evidence; no universal Roman institution or continuous use period is inferred.

stages.label: Gellone sacramentary manuscript
stages.scope: BnF Latin 12048's principal late eighth-century sacramentary state; later marginal and f. 1 additions excluded from the coordinate.
stages.summary: The BnF description dates the codex to the last quarter of the eighth century and describes a Frankish Gelasian sacramentary containing Frankish, Roman and Gregorian liturgical material, plus later additions.

evidence.locus: Date; Description, contents and f. 1 addition
evidence.claim: Identifies the copy date, mixed sacramentary character and a ninth-century addition at f. 1.

stages.limitations: The codex's physical extent is not a checked transcription or a complete reconstructed missal. The 1981 edition is modern scholarship. The catalogue's mixed-text description establishes neither exact donor books nor an archetype for other Frankish Gelasian witnesses.
stages.reception: The catalogue describes early Gellone ownership and use; no wider Frankish or Roman adoption is inferred.

stages.label: St Gall 348 (Remedius) Gelasian sacramentary
stages.date_label: manuscript copied at the turn of the eighth and ninth centuries (ELMSS 796–824; e-codices 'around 800')
stages.scope: The principal Rhaetian copy of St. Gallen, Stiftsbibliothek, Cod. Sang. 348, with its Canon; the front St Gall Masses, the Remedius commemoration and later St Gall corrections are distinguished as separate layers.
stages.summary: A Frankish Gelasian sacramentary titled as a liber sacramentorum anni circuli Romanae ecclesiae (p. 32), with the Roman Canon (p. 368). A contemporary red-capital entry at the foot of p. 368 commemorates Bishop Remedius of Chur; Masses for the vigil and feast of St Gall stand in another hand at the front (p. 10).

evidence.locus: pp. 32, 368 and 10; IIIF metadata; Scherrer 1875 p. 122 (TEI)
evidence.claim: Images show the incipit, the Canon with the Remedius commemoration keyed to the Te igitur, and St Gall Masses in another hand; the record places the book at St Gall by about 850.

evidence.locus: Date; Origin and Provenance; Script Commentary
evidence.claim: Dates the copying 796–824, places it probably at Chur, calls the Remedius entry contemporary, and reports correction throughout at St Gall in the second half of the ninth century.

stages.limitations: The 796–824 range dates the principal copy, not the composition of its prayers or a Frankish Gelasian archetype. The St Gall Masses and corrections are later, undated layers here, and no prayer-level comparison with Gellone, Rheinau or the Old Gelasian is made. Its relationship to St Gall 350 is not asserted.
stages.reception: The Remedius commemoration ties the book to the church of Chur around 800; the St Gall Masses and corrections show later use at St Gall. No wider Frankish adoption is inferred.

stages.label: Cambrai Hadrianum sacramentary copy
stages.date_label: early ninth century; precise copying date disputed
stages.scope: Cambrai MS 164 (159), an extant Hadrianum-family sacramentary, with copy date deliberately unpositioned pending resolution of catalogue disagreement.
stages.summary: USUARIUM identifies the codex and lists Ordinary, Canon and Mass-prayer material. Its 812–813 copy assertion is different from its proposed 790–800 Aachen master-copy date; the wider inventory records competing datings.

evidence.claim: Identifies the actual Cambrai codex and explicitly separates its reported 812–813 copying from the proposed earlier exemplar.

stages.limitations: No year coordinate is assigned while the competing 811/812, 812/813 and later palaeographic datings remain unresolved. The Roman exemplar sent to Charlemagne is not this extant codex; neither its date nor papal composition is assigned to the copy. Wilson 1915 and Lietzmann 1921 are modern editions.
stages.reception: A Frankish copy of a Gregorian sacramentary state; not proof of immediate universal replacement of Gelasian books.

stages.label: Trento Gregorian sacramentary witness
stages.scope: Trento cod. 1590 as an extant Gregorian sacramentary witness, with its supplement distinguished from the principal book.
stages.summary: The catalogue dates the manuscript to the first half of the ninth century and indexes a Mass Ordinary, Canon and annual prayers.

evidence.claim: Identifies the manuscript and its indexed Ordinary, Canon and prayer sequence.

stages.limitations: The 800–850 range dates the witness. The catalogue's Salzburg-model note is not an inspected exemplar or direction of borrowing. The 1985 critical edition is not a ninth-century reform, and the supplement has not been collated separately.
stages.reception: Local manuscript attestation only; no general Roman or Frankish adoption date established.

stages.label: Padua Gregorian sacramentary witness
stages.scope: Padua Cathedral MS D. 47's principal Gregorian sacramentary state, with corrector and later Verona appendix left undated.
stages.summary: USUARIUM dates the manuscript 830–870 and indexes Mass prayers and the Canon. It separately reports a compilation estimate of 840–855 and subsequent corrections and Verona additions.

evidence.claim: Identifies the manuscript, Mass and Canon contents, and the distinct appendix and correction notices.

stages.limitations: Copying range, compilation estimate and later correction are different events. The 1927 and 2005 critical editions are not medieval book states. Exact corrective changes and appendix date remain uncollated.
stages.reception: Manuscript witness with later Verona association; no inferred universal Roman use.

stages.label: Earlier Gallicanum Vetus sacramentary part
stages.date_label: ff. 1–18 copied in the first half of the eighth century (701–750)
stages.scope: The first sacramentary part of Vatican Pal. lat. 493, not the later bound composite as a single copied book.
stages.witness_label: Vatican Pal. lat. 493 ff. 1–18, ELMSS 104 / CLA 1.92
stages.summary: ELMSS identifies these eighteen folios as a French sacramentary copied in the first half of the eighth century and bound with another, later sacramentary.

evidence.locus: Shelfmarks; Date; Origin and Provenance; Contents
evidence.claim: Separately identifies and dates the first sacramentary part.
Original images show the first part beginning acephalously in a Mass for Germanus and ending at f. 18v mid-sentence in a creed exposition, in a large hand distinct from the following part.

stages.limitations: The aggregate 675–725 date in USUARIUM 957 cannot date this entire composite. Named folio images were checked, but no prayer collation; original composition, relation to the later part and binding date are unknown. Mohlberg 1958 is a modern edition.
stages.reception: A surviving Gallican sacramentary part; no universal Gallican rite or regional reception map follows.

stages.label: Later Gallicanum Vetus sacramentary part
stages.date_label: ff. 19–99 copied in the second half of the eighth century (751–800)
stages.scope: The second sacramentary part of Vatican Pal. lat. 493; later bound with ff. 1–18 and a non-sacramentary section.
stages.witness_label: Vatican Pal. lat. 493 ff. 19–99, ELMSS 105 / CLA 1.93
stages.summary: ELMSS identifies a distinct French sacramentary in the same modern binding and dates its script to the second half of the eighth century.

evidence.locus: Shelfmarks; Date; Origin and Provenance; Contents
evidence.claim: Separately identifies and dates the second sacramentary part.
Original images show the second part opening mid-prayer in a different script and layout, followed by the heading Incipit exorcismus.

stages.limitations: The later copy date does not mean this part revised the first. The textual break on both sides of ff. 18v/19r shows lost leaves of unknown number, not a relationship. No prayer collation, common exemplar, binding date or complete original book extent established. The later Decretum Gelasianum folios are not a third sacramentary stage.
stages.reception: A surviving Gallican sacramentary part; it does not establish a single uniform Gallican service book.

stages.label: Bobbio manuscript sacramentary core
stages.date_label: principal manuscript copied in the eighth century (701–800)
stages.scope: BnF Latin 13246's principal sacramentary text, with inserted and added material distinguished.
stages.witness_label: Paris BnF Latin 13246, the so-called Bobbio Missal
stages.summary: The manuscript catalogue identifies a Gallican sacramentary core, an inserted Mass on ff. 251–253 and added matter on other named folios. The 1917 facsimile plates show that the inserted Mass is a Mass for the ruler ('principem nostrum') in a different hand, and that f. 253v carries later cursive additions.

evidence.locus: Date; Contents; Script Commentary, ff. 251–253 and added folios
evidence.claim: Dates the witness and distinguishes principal script, inserted Mass and later added matter.

evidence.locus: Facsimile PDF 511–518 = ff. 250r–253v (folio numbers 251–253 photographed on PDF 513–517)
evidence.claim: The facsimile shows the main hand ending at f. 250v, a differently written Mass for a ruler on ff. 251r–253r beginning Deus regum atque cunctorum regnorum, and a later cursive hand on f. 253v.

stages.limitations: The 701–800 range is manuscript dating, not the composition of every prayer. Bobbio is the find place, while probable southeast French origin remains a catalogue judgment. Neither direct Celtic ancestry nor Besançon provenance is established. Lowe's 1917 facsimile publication is not an eighth-century stage.
stages.reception: A manuscript later found at Bobbio; no broader regional or ecclesial reception established.

stages.label: Stowe Mass and pastoral-rite manuscript core
stages.scope: RIA D.ii.3 ff. 12–67, the Mass, baptism and sick-communion book; separately bound Gospel excerpts and subsequent revisions distinguished.
stages.witness_label: Dublin Royal Irish Academy D.ii.3 ff. 12–67
stages.summary: ELMSS dates the Mass codex approximately to 792 and records numerous later additions. The RIA/DIAS catalogue distinguishes it from eleven Gospel folios bound with it and describes its Mass, baptism and sick-communion contents.

evidence.claim: Identifies ff. 12–67, approximate core date and later additions.
Distinguishes the Gospel portion from the Mass and pastoral-rite codex.

Original images show the Missal opening at f. 12r with a later upper-margin heading, and the signature Moel Caich scripsit closing the communion antiphons on f. 37r in a hand distinct from that of f. 37v.

stages.limitations: The narrower 780–820 ELMSS estimate concerns the core, whereas the aggregate inventory gives eighth–ninth centuries. The Máel Caích hand is now image-checked at its f. 37r signature, but the extent and date of that revision remain undetermined and uncollated. Warner 1906/1915 are facsimile and edition dates, not early liturgical dates; no universal Celtic rite is inferred.
stages.reception: An Irish manuscript witness with later Lorrha associations; no all-Ireland or modern Catholic authorization claim.

gaps.period: Before and after the Verona copy
gaps.missing: Original Verona codex image review, constituent libellus chronology and folio-level separation of the seventh-century continuation.
gaps.next_source: Verona Biblioteca Capitolare LXXXV (80) original images or a complete institutional facsimile, checked against ELMSS 866.
gaps.consequence: The copying date remains one attested collection state, without a dated Roman institutional origin or complete text.

gaps.period: Old Gelasian copy and textual strata
gaps.missing: Collation of the detached Paris ff. 41–56 against the Vatican volume, prayer-level collation beyond the six image-checked Vatican folios, and resolution of the competing BAV ('Sec. VIII in.') and ELMSS (726–775) copy datings and of composition strata.
gaps.next_source: BnF lat. 7193 ff. 41–56 images when Gallica is reachable; further DigiVatLib Reg. lat. 316 folios (Book III opening and Canon) compared with Wilson 1894 as a control edition; current palaeographic literature on the Chelles attribution.
gaps.consequence: One manuscript state is recorded with image-checked book divisions and explicit; papal authorship, strata dates and direct descent into Frankish Gelasian books remain unasserted.

gaps.period: Late eighth- and ninth-century Frankish Gelasian books
gaps.missing: Gellone additions, Rheinau 30, St Gall 350, Angoulême and other Frankish Gelasian codices have no image-checked stages; St Gall 348 now has one, but no prayer-level comparison among any of these witnesses exists.
gaps.next_source: BnF Latin 12048 and lat. 816 images (Gallica blocked on 2026-10-21); Zürich ZB Rh. 30 images (not found on e-codices or e-manuscripta); e-codices Cod. Sang. 350; compare named prayers across witnesses.
gaps.consequence: Gellone and St Gall 348 supply dated witnesses, not an archetype, reform transition or complete Frankish Gelasian line.

gaps.period: Pre-Hadrianic, Hadrianum and supplemented Gregorian transmission
gaps.missing: The dispatched Roman exemplar, Cambrai copy date disagreement, Padua corrector and Verona appendix, Trento supplement and exact relationships among witnesses remain unresolved.
gaps.next_source: Cambrai MS 164, Trento cod. 1590 and Padua D. 47 images or authoritative full manuscript catalogues; compare named components before drawing any transition.
gaps.consequence: The three extant codices are attested separately; no universal replacement, direct parentage or date for a particular supplementation is plotted.

gaps.period: Eighth-century parts and their later binding
gaps.missing: Binding date of Pal. lat. 493, the number of leaves lost on both sides of ff. 18v/19r, and any textual relation between the two image-checked sacramentary parts.
gaps.next_source: Heidelberg/Vatican codicological description of quiring and binding (the Heidelberg site requires an interactive bot check); Mohlberg 1958 introduction as a modern description, not a date.
gaps.consequence: Two copying states remain parallel; the observed scribal and textual break shows two incomplete books, not a revision or common archetype.

gaps.missing: Prayer-level comparison of the core with the inserted ruler's Mass (ff. 251–253) and the later added matter (ff. 1–8, 253v–254, 291v–295), and any date for those additions; current original images.
gaps.next_source: BnF Latin 13246 Gallica images (HTTP 403 on 2026-10-21); HBS 58 edited text and HBS 61 palaeographical notes for the hands of the added leaves.
gaps.consequence: The inserted Mass and later additions are image-distinguished layers of one copy, not a dated revision or Celtic/Gallican/Roman descent edge.

gaps.period: Stowe core and later Móel-Cáich work
gaps.missing: The extent of the Máel Caích additions and rewritten or inserted leaves beyond the image-checked f. 37r signature, and an independently defensible date for them.
gaps.next_source: Remaining ISOS RIA D.ii.3 folios compared hand by hand with Warner 1906 facsimile and 1915 edition annotations on the inserted Moelcaich quire.
gaps.consequence: The core has an approximate copy date and the revising hand is image-checked; the revision remains an unpositioned layer, not a dated stage.
